observations.fact: The H1 harness fixes context1024, batch512, UB1/128, greedy seed123 and cap128. It feeds prompt chunks to common_prompt_batch_decode and then one generated ID per call. This is source-level input/call structure, not an observed internal occupied-forward trace.

The retained instrumented native frontend calls target prefill on all prompt IDs except the last and then the last ID separately. Its alternate context is initialized with UB1/128 before decoding a sampled target block. These source calls do not establish old H1 internal state histories or a causal origin.

The existing observer uses llama_state_get_data/set_data between contexts and records length/content/consumption plus committed IDs and capacities. This provides an engineering starting point; transfer at a different phase and full sampler/pending-state consistency must be newly qualified.

diagnostic_hypothesis: A prospective diagnostic candidate may need to separate target prefill history from later target execution. This is not a discovered numerical cause, evidence that prefill caused the old divergences, or a validated candidate fix.
engineering_gaps: No dynamic UB setter assumed. A separate-context state transfer must be validated for the chosen phase, including output/pending-token and sampler ownership.
Do not infer actual backend microbatch shapes from UB capacity or caller token count. New instrumentation would be needed for those measurements.
Compact arrays lack the required native/reproducer full trace and raw state bytes; no omitted runtime/model/driver assets were retrieved.
